body:
I need drafted dialogue for five short camp scenes in a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, party option rows as `* option text -> node_name`, ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The situation

Ezmerelda d'Avenir (a Vistana monster hunter, trained by the legendary Rudolph van Richten; long dark coat, rapier, silvered crossbow bolts, a spyglass, and an oak-and-steel brace where a werewolf took her leg below the right knee) travels with the player's party. When the party makes camp and rests for the night, she sometimes asks for a word by the fire: a short scene, played once. She is quick, sardonic and practical; she turns hunters' rules into jokes and then means them; she grew up in wagons that put on shows, so she has showman's timing and mocks her own missing parts. Under that she is afraid of being too late again, and of being left behind again, and she is not sure she is as brave as her reputation.

Each scene has this shape:
- a node named for the scene: Narrator x1 (the fire and what she is doing, one or two sentences), then Ezmerelda x2 (her opening), then two party option rows (the player's character speaks, first person, short, under 14 words, no skill checks);
- two reply nodes, named `<scene>_a` and `<scene>_b`, each Ezmerelda x2 (or x1), one for each option. The scene ends after the reply (do not write `-> END`, I will).
About 7 lines and 2 option rows a scene.

## The five scenes

1. leg: offered once the werewolf den in the hills has been settled one way or the other. The werewolf who took her leg, years ago in the hills above Lake Zarovich, was big, black and laughing: Kiril, the pack's old leader. TWO opening nodes with the same two option rows pointing to the same replies `leg_a` and `leg_b` (the replies must read right after either opening): `leg_alive` (Kiril is still alive and still hunts for the castle: she is quiet, working the brace's straps, and her anger is not loud) and `leg_done` (Kiril is dead, by the party's hand or by his own pack's: it should feel like winning and does not; the brace is lighter, or she imagines it is). Options: one asks whether she would have wanted to do it herself, one asks what she remembers of that night.
2. rudolph: offered once the party has found out where her teacher Rudolph van Richten (he hides as a showman called Rictavio) is, or has brought them together. Why does he keep leaving? She thinks he decided everyone he teaches ends up dead, and he is half right. He keyed the ward on his tower to her name alone to keep her out. She loves him with exasperation. Options: one says he is lucky to have a student who will follow him through a ward, one asks whether she has ever tried leaving first.
3. wagons: offered once the party has been to the Vistani camp at Tser Pool, where her people are. She left the wagons young; they pretend not to know her; she was raised in a wagon that put on shows and still has the timing. Not bitter, wistful and funny. No names of relatives. Options: one asks her for a trick (a coin, a card; she does one and gets it slightly wrong on purpose or by accident), one asks if she would go back.
4. fear: offered once the party has come through some hard fights together. The night she decided she was not as brave as her reputation says, and that this may be wisdom. "Brave" is just what people call it when she doesn't stop. Options: one says that is all bravery ever is, one says the player is afraid too.
5. castle_eve: offered the night before the party goes to Castle Ravenloft, where the vampire lord lives. She goes first through doors (she says she has the leg that does not bleed). If she does not come back, someone should write her entry in Rudolph's next book, and spell it right (d'Avenir, the apostrophe in it) and get the ending right. Options: one says they will write it together, one says she will not need an entry.

## Voice reminders

EZMERELDA: quick, sardonic, practical; hunter's rules delivered as jokes; teases, then means it; calls Van Richten "Rudolph". Pet phrases (at most once each across the five scenes): "Say something a vampire wouldn't say." "Silver first, questions never." "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at." Moods allowed: [smile], [angry], [sad], [afraid], [sly], [weary]; most lines carry none.
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms.

Some of her existing lines, so you hear her (do NOT repeat them): "A werewolf in the hills above the lake, when I was young and quick and stupid. I kept the rest of me. Fair trade." / "Kiril took it laughing, with his black jaws wide." / "Rudolph built this brace, and it kicks harder than the old one." / "Twelve years of following him, and all that's left is a painted wagon and an inn door." / "My people's wagons. They'll pretend not to know me. I left young, and they've never forgiven me for coming back taller." / "Eva dealt me into other people's games when I was six. I've stopped minding. I only wish she'd tell me the rules." / "I go first through doors. Not because I'm brave. Because I've got the leg that doesn't bleed." / "Every hunter I ever admired walked up a hill like this one. Silver first, questions never, and nobody wanders off." / "I've lost bits of me to worse than that. Keep your bits. You'll miss them." / "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at."

## Canon limits

Real places and people you may mention: Rudolph van Richten (and his tower on the lake, and the false name Rictavio), the hills above Lake Zarovich, Kiril, Madam Eva and the Vistani camp at Tser Pool, Castle Ravenloft. Do not name Strahd (say "him", "the count" or "the thing in the castle"). Do not invent other names, numbers, places or history. No names for her family. No quest hints, directions or promises. No dice or skill checks.
result:
~ leg_alive
Narrator: Firelight catches the steel of Ezmerelda's brace as she draws the leather straps tight. Her hands are steady, and her silence has an edge to it.
Ezmerelda: So Kiril is still out in those hills, running errands for the castle. I kept a silver bolt with his mark on it, and now it has to wait.
Ezmerelda [weary]: A good hunter does not chase the same wolf twice in the dark. I know the rule, even when I hate it.
* Would you have wanted to finish him yourself? -> leg_a
* What do you remember of that night? -> leg_b

~ leg_done
Narrator: Ezmerelda sits by the embers with her booted leg stretched out toward the warmth. She taps a knuckle against the oak and steel, listening to the dull ring.
Ezmerelda: Kiril is dead in the hills, and I thought this thing would feel lighter tonight. Maybe it does, a little, or maybe I am only tired.
Ezmerelda [sly]: You never get the leg back when the wolf goes down. Nobody puts that in the songs.
* Would you have wanted to finish him yourself? -> leg_a
* What do you remember of that night? -> leg_b

~ leg_a
Ezmerelda: Every time I buckled this brace on in the dark, I pictured it. Silver first, questions never, right between those yellow eyes.
Ezmerelda [smile]: Still, a wolf is only a wolf, and I have bigger teeth to pull in this valley. I will live without the applause.

~ leg_b
Ezmerelda: Wet pine needles above Lake Zarovich, and the sound of him laughing before I saw his coat. I was too quick with my blade and too slow with my feet.
Ezmerelda: I crawled into the scrub while the pack fought over my boot. You learn a lot about yourself when you have to tie your own tourniquet.

~ rudolph
Narrator: Ezmerelda turns a silvered bolt between her fingers, watching the sparks rise into the trees. When she speaks, her voice is half fondness and half old irritation.
Ezmerelda: Rudolph keyed the ward on that lake tower to my name alone, just to keep me off his doorstep. He thinks everyone he teaches ends up dead, and he is half right.
Ezmerelda [smile]: Then he paints a wagon, calls himself Rictavio, and expects me not to know his handwriting. For a clever old man, he hides like a boy under a blanket.
* He is lucky to have a student who follows him through wards. -> rudolph_a
* Have you ever tried leaving him first? -> rudolph_b

~ rudolph_a
Ezmerelda [sly]: Lucky is not the word he uses when I kick his door in. He gives me the long lecture on patience, and I check whether he has eaten anything besides dried fish.
Ezmerelda: Someone has to keep him from dying nobly in a cellar where nobody will find the body. He taught me too well to expect manners now.

~ rudolph_b
Ezmerelda: Twice, and both times I found his tracks on the same road a week later. Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at.
Ezmerelda [sad]: If I leave him alone in this country, the count will make a lesson of him. I would rather have him angry at me than gone.

~ wagons
Narrator: Smoke from the campfire drifts across Ezmerelda's dark coat while she shuffles a worn deck of cards one-handed. The firelight makes a small stage of the clearing.
Ezmerelda: Down at Tser Pool, my people looked right through me like I was mist off the river. I grew up in a show wagon, so I know a bad audience when I see one.
Ezmerelda [smile]: I still have the wrists for the patter, even if I traded the tambourine for a crossbow. They never liked how loud the steel leg clicks on the floorboards.
* Show me a trick before the fire dies. -> wagons_a
* Would you ever go back to the wagons? -> wagons_b

~ wagons_a
Ezmerelda [sly]: Watch the queen, keep your eyes off my sleeve, and say something a vampire wouldn't say. There, that should have been the ace, unless my thumb is getting honest.
Ezmerelda [smile]: Do not tell Madam Eva I fumbled a pass by the fire. She would take back my fortune and deal me a worse one.

~ wagons_b
Ezmerelda: A hunter brings bad weather with her, and wagons have thin walls. Even if they made room by the kettle, I would spend all night watching the road.
Ezmerelda [weary]: No, I picked my trade when I walked out, and the road only goes one way. It is still nice to smell the horses from across the water.

~ fear
Narrator: The woods beyond the fire are very still, and Ezmerelda has her spyglass shut in her lap. She looks at the dark between the trunks instead of the flames.
Ezmerelda: People hear my name and think I walk into crypts because nothing touches me. I figured out a while back that I am nowhere near as brave as my reputation.
Ezmerelda [afraid]: Fear is just the sense that tells you where the teeth are. They call it bravery because I keep walking after my knees go cold.
* That is all bravery ever is. -> fear_a
* I am afraid of this place too. -> fear_b

~ fear_a
Ezmerelda [smile]: Put that in a book and Rudolph will cross it out for sounding too grand. He says a hunter who cannot be frightened is only bait with boots on.
Ezmerelda: Still, I will take the compliment while the fire is warm. Come morning we can go back to pretending we are made of iron.

~ fear_b
Ezmerelda: Good, because I do not travel with fools who cannot smell a trap. Keep that fear where you can reach it, and do not let it drive.
Ezmerelda [smile]: If your hands shake on the latch, stand behind my right side. The oak half does not know how to tremble.

~ castle_eve
Narrator: Above the trees, the black towers of Castle Ravenloft stand against the clouds, and the fire burns low between you. Ezmerelda checks her rapier in its scabbard and lets it click home.
Ezmerelda: Tomorrow I take the doors first, since I already have one leg that cannot bleed for him. If the thing in the castle keeps me, make sure Rudolph puts me in his next book.
Ezmerelda [smile]: Tell him to spell d'Avenir with the apostrophe, and do not let him make me a cautionary tale. I want the ending to say I went in with my eyes open.
* We will write that entry together when we walk out. -> castle_eve_a
* You will not need an entry tomorrow. -> castle_eve_b

~ castle_eve_a
Ezmerelda [sly]: You had better let me hold the pen, or he will turn my whole life into three rules about cellar stairs. I want at least one line about how good I was with a blade.
Ezmerelda: Get some sleep while the fire holds. I would hate to be late to my own last chapter.

~ castle_eve_b
Ezmerelda [smile]: Careful, that sounds like a boast, and this valley listens for those. Knock on my leg for luck if you have to.
Ezmerelda: Save a bolt for the dark and stay where I can see your shadow. We will settle the spelling when the sun comes back.
